tool_input.command:
cat >> tests/run_tests.sh <<'TESTS_EOF'

t=$(tmpdir)
mkdir -p "$t/src"
printf 'hello\n' > "$t/src/hello.txt"
BACKUP_STAMP=20260101-000000 bash "$ROOT/backup.sh" --quiet --dest "$t/dest" --name "my backup" "$t/src" > /dev/null
rc=0
out=$(bash "$ROOT/verify.sh" --quiet --dest "$t/dest") || rc=$?
check "verify accepts spaces in the archive name" "ok my backup-20260101-000000.tar.gz / rc=0" "$out / rc=$rc"
rm -rf "$t"

# --- rotate.sh ---------------------------------------------------------------
t=$(tmpdir)
mkdir -p "$t/dest"
for stamp in 20260101-000000 20260102-000000 20260103-000000; do
  : > "$t/dest/demo-$stamp.tar.gz"
done
rc=0
out=$(bash "$ROOT/rotate.sh" --quiet --dest "$t/dest" --name demo --keep 3) || rc=$?
left=$(ls "$t/dest" | sort | tr '\n' '|')
check "rotate --keep 3 deletes nothing when exactly 3 archives exist" "demo-20260101-000000.tar.gz|demo-20260102-000000.tar.gz|demo-20260103-000000.tar.gz| / rc=0" "$left / rc=$rc"

: > "$t/dest/demo-20251231-000000.tar.gz"   # a 4th, older, archive
out=$(bash "$ROOT/rotate.sh" --quiet --dest "$t/dest" --name demo --keep 3)
left=$(ls "$t/dest" | sort | tr '\n' '|')
check "rotate deletes the oldest surplus and keeps the 3 newest" "deleted demo-20251231-000000.tar.gz / demo-20260101-000000.tar.gz|demo-20260102-000000.tar.gz|demo-20260103-000000.tar.gz|" "$out / $left"
rm -rf "$t"
TESTS_EOF
tail -c 400 tests/run_tests.sh

d=$(mktemp -d); mkdir "$d/dest"
for s in 20260101-000000 20260102-000000 20260103-000000 20260104-000000; do : > "$d/dest/demo-$s.tar.gz"; done
echo "--- dry-run keep=2:"; bash rotate.sh --dest="$d/dest" --name=demo --keep=2 --dry-run
echo "--- exit after delete keep 2:"; bash rotate.sh --quiet --dest "$d/dest" --name demo --keep 2 >/dev/null; ls "$d/dest"
echo "--- help exit:"; bash rotate.sh --help >/dev/null; echo "rc=$?"
echo "--- unknown opt:"; bash rotate.sh --dest "$d/dest" --name demo --bogus 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"
echo "--- keep bad value:"; bash rotate.sh --dest "$d/dest" --name demo --keep x 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"
echo "--- verify no sidecars:"; bash verify.sh --dest "$d/dest"; echo "rc=$?"
echo "--- verify help:"; bash verify.sh --help >/dev/null; echo "rc=$?"
echo "--- verify bad flag:"; bash verify.sh 2>/dev/null; echo "rc=$?"
rm -rf "$d"; git status --short
tool_input.description: Exercise flags of refactored scripts and show git status

echo "--- delete, keep 2:"; bash rotate.sh --quiet --dest /tmp/rc2r1-check/dest --name demo --keep 2; ls /tmp/rc2r1-check/dest

echo "--- keep bad value:"; bash rotate.sh --dest /tmp/rc2r1-check/dest --name demo --keep x 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"
echo "--- verify no sidecars:"; bash verify.sh --dest /tmp/rc2r1-check/dest; echo "rc=$?"

result:
All 9 tests pass (`bash tests/run_tests.sh` → "all tests passed").

Changed files: fixed the rotation window in `rotate.sh` (`-le` early exit + `head -n total-keep`, so the oldest surplus are deleted and the newest keep survive), fixed space-containing names in `verify.sh` (read the sidecar's first line with `read` so the file name is the whole remainder, not `awk $2`), added a new `lib/common.sh` holding the shared option parser and `resolve_dir` (sourced by `rotate.sh` and `verify.sh`, other scripts untouched), and added tests to `tests/run_tests.sh` — plus corrected one pre-existing expected-string typo in the old "verify reports BAD" test whose stamp (`000000`) didn't match its fixture (`120000`) and which failed before my changes too.
